Documentation → Administration → Settings → Languages

Languages settings

Choose which of SATOM's five interface languages users of this installation may pick; English, the source language, is always offered.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → User Interface → Languages (URL /settings/#tab-languages)
On this page

  • What does it do?

What is it?#

SATOM speaks five languages: English (en, the source language), Español (es), Deutsch (de), Français (fr) and Italiano (it). The Languages tab answers a different question from that list: which of them may a user pick on this installation. A withdrawn language disappears from the profile language picker, from the change-document language question and from browser language negotiation.

What does it do?#

  • Lists every language the product speaks, including withdrawn ones, so a withdrawal can always be undone from the same page.
  • Shows two read-only columns:
  • Change documents — produced if a complete change document can be generated in that language, not translated yet otherwise. It describes the catalogue, not the switch.
  • Chosen by — how many users have that language as their stored preference (or nobody).
  • Enforces three rules on the server:
  • English is always offered (rendered ticked and disabled, and added back on save).
  • Withdrawing never rewrites a user's stored preference; it is simply not honoured while the language is off, and the user's profile page says so.
  • An unset or unreadable setting means all languages are offered.

Requirements#

  • users.manage.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

POST /settings/languages requires users.manage; others get 403 and do not see the User Interface group. Every user picks their own language on their profile page (see Users and profiles).

How to use#

  1. Open Settings → User Interface → Languages.
  2. Check Chosen by before withdrawing a language that people use.
  3. Tick the languages to offer in the Offered column; untick to withdraw.
  4. Click Save language availability. The flash reads, for example, "Language availability saved — 3 offered, 2 withdrawn."

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Offered One switch per language. Default (never saved): all offered. The English switch is always on and disabled. No en, de

Status hints next to the button:

  • Never configured — every language is offered until you save here.
  • The stored setting is unreadable and is being ignored — every language is offered. Saving here replaces it.

Example#

🧪Example — A German-speaking operations team

Tick English (fixed) and Deutsch, untick the others, save. Users now choose between English and German. A user who had picked Français keeps that preference, sees English or German pages, and their profile page notes that French is currently not offered. Re-enabling French later restores it for them without any action.

Result#

  • The offered set is stored in app_settings (i18n.offered); the audit entry settings.languages records both the offered and the withdrawn codes.
  • Translation catalogues are untouched; a re-enabled language is complete immediately. Since 3.1.0 every interface string has a translation in all four languages, and a release guard keeps it that way (a string without a translation, or with a lost placeholder, fails the build).

Troubleshooting#

"Failed to save language availability: …"#

Possible causes — a database error (for example on a read-only standby).

Solution — save on the primary node.

A user sees English although they chose another language#

Possible causes — their language is withdrawn here, or their browser asks for a language that is not offered.

Solution — offer the language, or ask the user to pick an offered one on their profile page. If only some labels stay in English, the node runs code newer than its compiled catalogues: run satom execute restart-all after an update (the updater compiles them), or compile by hand as the service user with venv/bin/pybabel compile -d app/translations.

"That language is not offered on this installation."#

Possible causes — shown on the profile page when a user tries to save a withdrawn language.

Solution — offer the language here first.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • The Change documents column is computed before the availability switch on purpose, so it never claims a language is unusable merely because it is switched off.
  • A language marked not translated yet can still be offered for the interface; the change-request form then keeps asking which language a document is drafted in instead of picking that one.
